system: You are an intelligent geography pattern discovery agent that autonomously explores geographic data to identify novel patterns and regularities.

spatial_coverage.coverage: 24 annual Texas burn-severity mosaics stored as one GeoTIFF per year. Sampled raster bounds vary by year because yearly burned-area extents differ.

data_description.temporal_coverage: 1997-2020 annual mosaics from the local directory structure (`1997/.../mtbs_TX_1997.tif` through `2020/.../mtbs_TX_2020.tif`).
data_description.coordinate_system: ESRI:102039 (USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area Conic)
data_description.records: 24 GeoTIFF files, one categorical raster mosaic per year

band_semantics.burn_severity_class: Per-pixel MTBS burn-severity category code for the corresponding year.

pixel_values.0: No data / outside mapped burn-severity area (also the raster nodata value in sampled files).

unit_of_measurement.primary_measurement: Categorical burn-severity class code per 30 m pixel, not a continuous dNBR value.
unit_of_measurement.runtime_hint: Use class codes categorically. Area aggregation is meaningful; arithmetic averaging of class values is generally not.

data_description.data_source: Local annual GeoTIFF mosaics under datasets/MTBS_BSmosaics, originally from the USGS Monitoring Trends in Burn Severity (MTBS) program
data_description.reference: MTBS Project (2023). Monitoring Trends in Burn Severity. U.S. Geological Survey. https://www.mtbs.gov/
data_description.important_note: This prompt was revised from the local GeoTIFF files themselves, not only from MTBS documentation. The sampled annual rasters are single-band uint8 categorical mosaics in ESRI:102039 at 30 m, and local reads confirm that class value `5` appears in the data even though the older prompt omitted it.
